public_rationale: Marcus calls this his 'hunch' and says any AI harm 'will be on his hands, and his reputation.' Part of that is a moral judgment about responsibility, which evidence cannot settle. The rest is a loose forecast with no deadline, no measure of reputation, and an open-ended set of triggers ('anything that goes wrong'). My searches found no polling that ties specific post-order AI harms to Trump's standing. Even with such polling, the words give no threshold for when blame counts as 'on his hands.' So the claim cannot be fairly scored either way.
limitations: A narrower reading (polls show Trump blamed for a named AI harm) could become checkable later, but the speaker did not commit to that.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Any AI-related harms that occur (cybercrime, bioweapons, teen suicides) will be attributed to Trump and damage his reputation.
conditions: if AI harms such as cybercrime, bioweapons attacks, or teen suicides occur

statement.excerpt: Anything that goes wrong, from AI-fueled cybercrime to bioweapons attacks facilitated by AI to teen suicides apparently linked to GenAI will be on his hands, and his reputation.

from_speaker: teen suicides apparently linked to GenAI

our_interpretation: The claim mixes a moral judgment ('on his hands') with a loose forecast that Trump's reputation will suffer from any AI harm. It names no deadline, no measure of blame or reputation, and no threshold.
A testable version would need polling or reporting that ties specific post-order AI harms to Trump. The words give no way to say when such blame would count as enough, or by when.
criteria.support_condition: Credible polling or reporting, after a specific AI-linked harm, showing the public broadly holds Trump responsible and that his standing fell because of it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Major AI-linked harms occur and polling or reporting shows the public does not blame Trump or his standing is unaffected, over a period long enough to be fair to the claim.
